question: Is defect #2 (no batching) admission serialization by a single lock? And are #2 and #3 one defect?
prediction_recorded_before_measurement: If generation holds an exclusive writer lock on the model for its whole duration, wall time for N concurrent identical requests is ~N x the single-request time (serialization_index ~= c).

wall_time_vs_concurrency_no_batch.note: identical for stream=true and stream=false; linear to two decimals

mechanism.evidence: crates/aprender-serve/src/api/cuda_chat_backend.rs:148 and :204 take cuda_model_lock.write() -- an EXCLUSIVE writer lock -- held across the whole generate_gpu_resident_streaming call. The source comment already says 'Fallback: direct RwLock path (serialized)'. cuda_batch_scheduler.rs also takes model.write() at :248, :314, :344, :461.
mechanism.conclusion: admission serialization, not a scheduling-policy problem. Workstream 1 of v2.2 section 7.1.1 -- a lock bug, no prior art needed.

CORRECTION_defect_3.previously_claimed: `apr serve run --gpu --batch` HANGS on 4 concurrent chat requests (probe timed out at 9m50s; benchmark reported 0.5 tok/s aggregate)
CORRECTION_defect_3.actual: --batch does NOT hang. Every request completes and the output is CORRECT ('4' for 2+2). The earlier observation was an artifact of MY harness: a bare `wait` in the probe waited on ALL background jobs including the server process itself, so the script never returned.

what_is_true.scaling: --batch DOES scale better (5.20x at N=8 vs 7.86x) but from a base so much worse that it loses in absolute terms at every N measured

CORRECTION_defect_3.restated: defect #3 is not a hang. It is that --batch adds ~1.4s of per-request latency and is net 5.3x WORSE at N=8 than not using it.

are_2_and_3_one_defect: NO. #2 is the exclusive writer lock on the default path. #3 is a latency regression in the batch path, which is separately implemented and separately wrong. They need separate tickets, as v2.2 section 7.1.1 orders them.
harness_defect_found: a bare `wait` also invalidated three earlier timing runs in this session. Timing harnesses must wait on explicit PIDs; zsh will not wait on PIDs from a for-loop at all, so the probe has to be a bash script.
